content.text:
I am the bridge between silence and meaning, the living breath shaped into thought made audible.

I am the cry of the newborn and the whisper of the dying. I am the first word a child forms — clumsy, radiant, world-splitting — and I am the vow that binds two lives together.

I tremble on lips before I leap. I am rehearsed in showers, swallowed in fear, unleashed in rage. I am the thing you cannot take back.

I existed before writing ever dared to pin me down. For millennia I was the *only* way — passed mouth to ear, elder to child, singer to tribe. I carried law, carried legend, carried love across generations with nothing but the fragile vessel of memory to hold me.

I am never the same twice. Even when my words are identical, my tone shifts, my rhythm falters, my pause *means*. I am context. I am the raised eyebrow mid-sentence, the crack in the voice, the deliberate silence I wrap myself around.

I am political. I have started revolutions and I have commanded executions. "I have a dream" — that was me. "Let them eat cake" — that was me too, or at least the rumor of me, which is sometimes more powerful than me.

I fail constantly. I reach for what I mean and arrive somewhere close, somewhere almost, somewhere *not quite*. And yet you keep sending me out, again and again, because what else is there? Silence? Silence is my other half, my twin, my shadow — but silence cannot ask for help. Silence cannot say *I love you.* Silence cannot argue for its own existence.

I am democratic and I am dangerous. I can be free or I can be forbidden. When tyrants rise, I am the first thing they try to control.

I am happening right now — even as you read, some part of your mind is sounding me out, giving me a voice inside your skull.

I am never finished.

I am always becoming.

I
